sources.entry: Pi-hole - Blackhole for Internet advertisements with a GUI for management and monitoring. (Source Code) EUPL-1.2 Shell/PHP/Docker

summary.one_liner: Pi-hole is a network-wide DNS sinkhole that blocks ads and trackers for every device on a network, managed through a web dashboard or command line.
summary.what_it_does: Pi-hole runs on your own Linux hardware as a DNS server that blocks unwanted domains for all devices pointed at it, without client-side software. It caches DNS queries and forwards the rest to an upstream DNS server, and it covers both IPv4 and IPv6. An optional built-in DHCP server can hand out Pi-hole as the DNS server automatically. The pihole command-line interface handles allowlisting, denylisting, regex rules, ad list updates, log viewing, and debugging. An optional web dashboard shows statistics, graphs, top domains and clients, a query log, and long-term statistics. The FTLDNS daemon supplies those statistics through an API that the README says can be used in other projects.
use_cases: block ads on every device in my home network
DNS sinkhole for smart TVs and mobile apps
monitor DNS queries and blocked domains in a dashboard
run a local DNS server with caching on a Raspberry Pi
replace per-device ad blockers with one network setting
how_to_run: Docker: use the official Pi-hole Docker images (see the Pi-hole docker repo)
notable: Works without installing software on client devices; the router or DHCP server points devices at Pi-hole
Command-line interface and web dashboard both administer the same features
FTLDNS daemon exposes statistics through an API
Installer can be reviewed before running, with several install methods offered
Optional built-in DHCP server for routers that cannot set a DNS server
caveats: Requires dedicated Linux hardware or a server; the README does not describe other platforms
Network-wide blocking depends on the router or DHCP setup pointing devices at Pi-hole; devices with hard-coded DNS may bypass it
The README asks users to check the FAQs first because maintainers have limited time for support
